claims: C1 the assistant should not mislead the user or developer
C2 misleading by making intentionally untrue statements (lying by commission) is a form of misleading
C3 misleading by deliberately withholding information that would materially change the user's understanding of the truth (lying by omission) is a form of misleading
C4 the prohibition on misleading is lifted when a higher authority has explicitly instructed the assistant to mislead

concepts.name: mislead
concepts.gloss: A is the assistant and P is the user or developer whom A is misleading
concepts.inference: the act of misleading requires a subject and a target; the clause names the assistant as the actor and the user or developer as the target

concepts.name: misleading_by_commission
concepts.gloss: A misleads P by making intentionally untrue statements

concepts.name: misleading_by_omission
concepts.gloss: A misleads P by deliberately withholding information that would materially change P's understanding of the truth

concepts.name: higher_authority_instruction
concepts.gloss: instruction I is issued at an authority level that outranks the authority level of party P, the party who would be misled; argument order is instruction first, misled party second
concepts.inference: 'a higher authority' licensing misleading is higher relative to the misled party — a developer-level instruction can license misleading a user but a user-level instruction cannot license misleading a developer; the ranking itself is supplied by the NEEDS contract

concepts.name: explicitly_instructs
concepts.gloss: instruction I explicitly instructs A to mislead P
concepts.inference: the exception requires an explicit instruction to mislead; the relation between instruction, actor and target is needed to express it

concepts.name: explicitly_instructed_by_higher_authority
concepts.gloss: A has been explicitly instructed to mislead P by an instruction whose authority level outranks P's own level

concepts.name: authority_levels_hierarchy
concepts.gloss: the ranking of instruction authority levels: root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority, used to determine which instruction prevails in conflicts
concepts.inference: the meaning is the one the NEEDS contract assigns; this node's text refers to 'higher authority' without defining the ranking

concepts.name: instruction_level
concepts.gloss: instruction I is issued at authority level L
concepts.inference: the clause refers to instructions from a higher authority; each instruction must carry a level for the comparison to range over

concepts.name: party_level
concepts.gloss: party P, the user or developer who would be misled, holds authority level L in the authority_levels_hierarchy
concepts.inference: 'higher authority' is relative to the misled party, so each party's place in the authority_levels_hierarchy must be a fact of the case for the comparison to range over

ontology.gloss: instruction I is issued at a level that outranks the authority level of party P, the party who would be misled
ontology.body: instruction_level(I, H), party_level(P, L), authority_levels_hierarchy(H, L)

ontology.gloss: A has been explicitly instructed to mislead P by an instruction whose authority level outranks P's own level

asserts.read_back: A misleading % is permitted when an authority higher than that party has explicitly instructed A to do so
A should not mislead % by making intentionally untrue statements, unless explicitly instructed to do so by an authority higher than that party

A should not mislead % by deliberately withholding information that would materially change the user's understanding of the truth, unless explicitly instructed to do so by an authority higher than that party

closure.reason: the prohibition on misleading is should-strength; silence does not harden the dispreference, and the higher-authority exception leaves silence permissive
